title: What is Digital Identity? A Transdisciplinary Meta-synthesis
main_constructs: digital identity; online identity; context; agency; system mechanisms; social selfhood
notes: Explicitly distinguishes digital identity as system mechanisms from online identity as social selfhood; highly relevant to scope separation.

title: A Social Identity Theory of Digital Identity
main_constructs: social digital identity; online/offline group membership; identity salience; social roles; digital platforms
notes: Shows a mature psychological research lane connecting group identity and digital identity without implying IAM/federation semantics.

title: Social Identity Theory and Self-categorization Theory: A Historical Review
main_constructs: social identity; self-categorization; group processes; ingroup/outgroup
notes: Foundational social-identity theory is group/self-concept oriented, not digital identity management.

title: Social Psychology of Identities
main_constructs: social bases of identity; multiple identities; social construction; intersection; virtual identity
notes: Supports multidimensional, socially situated identities and distinguishes this research object from technical identity records.

title: The Past, Present, and Future of an Identity Theory
main_constructs: role identity; social structure; self-verification; identity commitment
notes: Useful for role identity and self-verification; should not be merged with IAM role or interaction role.

title: Identity Theory: Progress in Relating the Two Strands
venue: New Directions in Identity Theory and Research
main_constructs: multiple identities; identity bases; salience; commitment; identity change
notes: Reinforces multiple/salient role identities and lifecycle-like identity change but in a psychosocial sense.

title: From Social to Political Identity: A Critical Examination of Social Identity Theory
main_constructs: identity choice; subjective meaning; identity strength; stability; political identity
notes: Highlights identity strength and subjective meaning, constructs outside CM4DI technical Core.

title: Social Influence and Group Identity
main_constructs: group identity; norms; social influence; anonymity; visibility; online context
notes: Shows online context can modulate social-identity processes; this is not equivalent to IdentityContext in IAM.

title: Digital identity formation: socially being real and present on digital networks
main_constructs: online identity formation; self-presentation; self-disclosure; social presence
notes: Useful for persona/presentation boundary; technical DigitalIdentity should not subsume self-presentation.

title: Context collapse: theorizing context collusions and collisions
main_constructs: context collapse; public/private; multiple selves; audience
notes: Demonstrates that social context/audience has richer semantics than CM4DI IdentityContext.

title: Self-transformation online through alternative presentations of self: a review, critique, and call for research
venue: Annals of the International Communication Association
main_constructs: self-presentation; alternative self; avatar; persona; identity shift
notes: Strong evidence that persona/self-presentation is a separate social/psychological construct family.

title: Unified Foundational Ontology (UFO) social entities and roles
main_constructs: social agent; social role; normative description; social relator; commitment
notes: Provides a principled bridge for future social-role ontology work; CM4DI should reuse grounding rather than reinvent social-role semantics.

title: The Organization Ontology
main_constructs: organization; membership; role; post; affiliation; temporal membership
notes: Shows mature reusable semantics for affiliation/membership and role-in-organization; prefer mapping/linking over CM4DI Core duplication.

title: SDHSS Social Life Core
main_constructs: social perception; social relationship; membership; social role; social quality; religious identity
notes: Demonstrates that a dedicated social-life ontology requires constructs substantially beyond digital identity management and supports an independent future track.
